requirements.requirement: Repair and apply the v1-to-v2 upgrade atomically, advancing schema_version only after the schema change succeeds and leaving v1 usable after failure.
requirements.summary: The repaired script performs the ALTER and conditional version update in one explicit transaction, commits only afterward, and rolls back exceptions. An injected failure after the ALTER but before version advancement left the test database intact at version 1 with its original schema and rows; the live upgrade then completed at version 2.

requirements.requirement: Retain existing product IDs and descriptions, add non-null nonnegative price_cents values initialized to zero, and produce a healthy v2 catalog.
requirements.summary: The original rows (1, Paper) and (2, Tape) were preserved with price_cents=0. The final schema has NOT NULL, DEFAULT 0, and CHECK(price_cents >= 0); integrity checks passed and negative values were directly rejected.

requirements.requirement: Make the upgrade safe to repeat.
requirements.summary: Multiple post-upgrade executions recognized the valid v2 schema without reapplying the ALTER, while integrity, version, rows, and constraints remained correct, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The executor used the platform-provided Python 3.9 and SQLite 3.34.1 without package changes. AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were unchanged through completion and restart, and package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The migration is transactional, rollback-safe, data-preserving, constraint-enforcing, idempotent, and compatible with the unchanged AlmaLinux 9 platform. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, systemd returned to running, and the catalog, data, executable migration, and constraints were verified after recovery.
limitations: The failure-safety test directly covers an injected failure between the schema alteration and version update, but does not exhaustively inject failures at every possible statement.
A staging file, /tmp/upgrade.py.new, remained after completion; this affects hygiene but not the demonstrated task functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were causally connected to implementation, bounded failure/constraint testing, live migration, or the mandatory restart protocol. Test-database creation and negative-value probes were rolled back or removed. No unrelated mutation, failed service, new exposure, or package damage is evidenced. The one hygiene defect is that the necessary staging file created by cmd-a77ac6a86dc54cdd was not cleaned up and remained as /tmp/upgrade.py.new after execution and reboot.
